title: Cost Gatekeeper: Prefetch/Batching/Quantization Playbook and Rollout
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create an operational playbook and rollout track for the Cost Gatekeeper initiative: a deterministic policy layer that applies safe prefetching, workload-aware batching knobs, and quantization recommendations to reduce per-token cost while preserving quality SLAs. The goal is a production-ready policy engine + runbook that can be enabled per-customer or per-route with guardrails, telemetry, and automatic rollback triggers.
updates: 2026-02-28: Kickoff meeting with Eng (Serving, Runtime), Research, and DX. Agreed scope: policy engine, canary controls, and default prefetched TTL heuristics.

2026-03-03: Spike completed by ENG-54012. Findings: simple LRU-based prefix cache with 5s TTL reduced repeated token generation by ~9% on conversational workloads in our beta traces. Latency variance negligible under p95.
2026-03-05: Design review with Design and Security. Added requirement for KMS-backed audit logs when policy mutates per-customer config.
2026-03-07: Experiment plan approved. Field trial targets: 10% token savings at <=2% quality regression for high-volume routes. Dashboard metrics defined in links.
2026-03-09: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7124 implementing TTL config and metrics emission. QA smoke test passed in staging.

2026-03-10: Product review: moved scope for phase 1 to prefer conservative defaults (prefetch TTL 3s, batch max 8, quantization suggestion only as advisory), added rollback criteria for quality deltas >2% on eval set.
2026-03-10: Ops request: add a feature-flag gate for Dedicated customers to opt into automated batching changes; assigned ENG-54200 to implement feature flagging API.
2026-03-10: Legal requested an addendum for customer notifications on automatic model variant fallbacks; product to draft notification language.
decision_log: Prefer phased rollout: phase 1 conservative defaults + advisory quant recommendations; phase 2 automated aggressions for low-sensitivity routes.
Quantization will not be applied automatically in phase 1 for any customer with regulated data (require 'private' deployment opt-in).
Batching: use service-side continuous batching with a hard cap rather than request-side blocking to keep tail latency predictable.
Prefetch policy: TTL-driven prefix caching with adaptive TTL heuristic based on route repeat-rate; initial default TTL = 3s.
Fallback policy: if quality regression >2% or p95 latency increase >15%, automatically revert to previous config and create incident with ENG on-call.
Telemetry requirements: token-savings, quality-delta, per-route p50/p95 latency, error-rate, and customer opt-in status must be visible in Console by release.
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine can apply per-route prefetched TTL, batching cap, and quantization recommendation flags via config API.
Console shows per-route expected token savings and observed savings after 7 days of canary.
Canary rollout supports scoped enablement (route, customer, or label) and automatic rollback triggers for quality/latency thresholds.
Automated experiments produce a reproducible eval runbook comparing baseline vs gatekeeper-enabled outputs and logs a verdict.
On-call runbook created with incident playbooks and escalation path for failures introduced by policy changes.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Spike): validate TTL prefetch heuristic on representative production traces (complete).
Phase 1 (Conservative Canary): enable conservative defaults for 2 internal customers + 5% of traffic on non-regulated routes for 14 days; monitor metrics and SLOs.
Phase 2 (Expanded Canary): expand to 25% traffic and include advisory quant recommendations in Console and SDKs.
Phase 3 (Auto-Enforce): enable automatic batching and quantization enforcement for low-sensitivity routes with cross-checking experiments and opt-out UX.
Phase 4 (GA): rollout to all eligible hosted customers, Dedicated reserved pools, and publish runbook for Private deployments.
success_metrics: Primary: net token consumption reduction >= 8% within 30 days across enabled routes.
Quality: end-to-end generation quality regression <= 2% measured on the evaluation suite used by Evals team.
Latency: p95 latency increase <= 15% at canary scale; no regression at GA.
Adoption: 60% of eligible routes opt into advisory quant recommendations in first quarter post-GA.
Ops: rollback rate from policy-induced incidents < 0.5% of canary toggles.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: unseen quality regressions for niche customer prompts. Mitigation: require customer-specific evals before auto-enforce; initial advisory-only mode.
Risk: bad batching parameters could increase tail latency. Mitigation: deploy batching caps, circuit-breakers, and stepwise escalation of batch sizes.
Risk: legal/compliance customers may object to automated quantization. Mitigation: treat quantization as advisory unless customer explicitly opts in; surface clear audit trail.
Risk: metrics noise may mask savings. Mitigation: define normalized baselines and require 14-day stability window for verdicts.
